decks.title: Replicating Dr. GRPO
decks.summary_easy: Tanay retrained Qwen2.5-1.5B on math problems with reinforcement learning, once with GRPO and once with Dr. GRPO, a 2025 fix that claims to stop wrong answers from getting longer without hurting accuracy. Using the paper's own data and grader, accuracy held (51.6% vs 51.2% on MATH500) but both length claims came out reversed. It is one seed and 100 short training steps, so Tanay reports it as not reproduced here rather than refuted.
decks.blurb: RL post training for math reasoning: the accuracy claim held and both length claims came out reversed.

decks.title: ZTF Transient Pipeline
decks.summary_easy: A nightly pipeline over real telescope alerts from the Zwicky Transient Facility: alerts are replayed through a Kafka broker, scored by a small image plus table classifier, and landed in a DuckDB warehouse, where dbt turns them into tested tables. Tanay ran it on 27,378 real alerts from July 20, 2026 and pushed 500 all the way through, with every dbt model and test passing. The plumbing and data contracts are real; the classifier is a smoke test model, not a science result.
decks.blurb: Real time astronomical alert classification on Kafka and Avro, with a dbt warehouse and drift checks.

decks.title: Gravity Spy 2.0 Research Assistant
decks.summary_easy: Tanay is a research assistant on Gravity Spy 2.0, an NSF funded citizen science project that helps LIGO find which detector hardware causes the noise bursts, called glitches, in gravitational wave data. Tanay built the pipeline that cleans more than 276,000 volunteer classifications and trained a neural network that predicts whether volunteers will call a sensor's signal similar to a glitch. The model ranks pairs well (0.89 AUC against volunteer labels), and its calibration error, the gap between its confidence and how often it is right, was cut in half, which matters more for how the scores will be used.
decks.blurb: LIGO glitch data: five schemas reconciled, 49,000 spectrograms, a calibrated two input CNN.

decks.title: JMA Wireless Lean Six Sigma Lead
decks.summary_easy: From January to May 2026, Tanay led a four person Lean Six Sigma team at JMA Wireless, a cell tower equipment maker, in the department that builds jumper cables. The team got five performance measures defined the same way for a manual line and an automated cell, built the data pipeline and dashboard, and found that the automated cell was almost never broken but was starved of parts. A daily standup Tanay piloted cut the time to act on a red measure from about four hours to about 25 minutes, and the projected value is about $355,000 a year pending the company's finance team.
decks.blurb: Five factory KPIs standardized, a 31 GB pipeline flattened, and the real constraint found upstream.
